svg.title: PMU box - plan sheet
svg.text: State: planned - its CAD is Y69. Rulings: D-596 D-597 D-599 D-600 D-601 D-603 D-604 D-606 D-607 D-610. Part folder: 00-design/pmu/
under the dash, driver-side footwell, its lid reachable for the fuses and its plugs facing down or sideways
(rules water-ingress) - the space assumed until M-1 (D-603)
Its board, enclosure and heat budget are the CAD pass's (Y69).

the PMU-24 DL on its own 39-way plug, its case one outside wall (D-596); eight smart high-side switches in place of K1-K4, K11, K12, K14, K15 and K13 a relay in a socket (D-597, D-352); the windows' two H-bridges in

place of K5-K8 (D-610); the big-fuse bank F30, F31, F32, F35, F36 and the mini-blade bank F1, F2, F3, F5, F12, F13, F15, F16, F19, F20, F21, F22, F23, F24, F33, F37 (D-597, D-599); the wake circuit (wake_stages) and the A15 /
A16 pull-ups, the oil-pressure pull-up with A7's tap, the pop-up diodes, the main-feed TVS (P136), the ground star; at the LS swap the ECU, the EMU PRO, on its own pigtails (D-601)

plugs L1-E1, L1-E2, L1-E3 (engine, wired for the LS from day one, D-606, D-607), L2-F1 (front), L4-R1 (rear); hard-wired, with a plug only at the far end: L3-COL, L3-DASH, L3-HU and the links to DP-ICU, DP-DCU, DP-DCU-P,
DP-CUR, L3-SD, L3-SP, D1, D2, DP-DIAG, L3-BLW, L3-MOD; the 2 AWG feed on a stud; one heavy ground lead from its star to a chassis ground point outside it (D-603)
Key supply — ignition switch B terminal (and through it the K13 back-stop coil) — L3-COL 10. The light switch
common and the brake-wake plunger branch off it behind the column through their own fuse, F24 (D-410, D-412)
Interior / spot lamp H-06 - L4-R1 12, always-hot as the factory had it; the lamp's own DOOR / OFF / ON switch
Two held consumers, no fuse this build: L3-MOD 1 → L3-MOD 1, the future module (D-274, kept by D-350) - the
TPMS receiver of D-318 is one such consumer, fed here and spliced onto CAN2 at the node when fitted (R16); and
L2-F1 12, a self-parking wiper motor's park feed (D-317). Always-hot - the bank's always-hot side
The display's backlight, ignition — DP-ICU 3 through the ICU carrier (D-268)
The AEM wideband gauge's own feed inside the DU, DP-ICU 18 (D-596; 5 A as AEM's sheet asks, SP-1734)
Wake stages' excitation rail (the door and A8 stages) — split off F3 by D-410
Light switch E-01 common and the brake-wake plunger, by their own wire L3-COL 11 (D-599)
L1-E1 12 (N68), the phase-2 sensor supply (D-271) - no fuse this build, fitted with the sensor
K3 / K4 terminals 30 and 86 - the hatch and fuel-door solenoids (L4-R1 7 / 8) and the two select coils, so a solenoid
cannot trip O10 and the cluster with it (D-465); CK20 measures the solenoids and may revise the rating
Driver seat power feed: K14 30 → L3-SD 1 (N106, N108). D-469 said about 30 A; 25 A is what the 12 AWG in the L3
bundle and the DTP size-12 contact carry (awg table, series) - seat motors draw 10-20 A
Passenger seat power feed: K15 30 → L3-SP 1 (N107, N109) - as F35
K1 / K2 terminal 30 - the 12 V the changeovers steer to R or RY, the four commands into the motors' own relays
(N12-N15 → L2-F1 13 / 14 / 17 and L2-F1 4). The commands are coil currents, under 0.5 A for both motors (SP-584;
CK08 reads it), on 14 AWG and DT size-16 contacts, so a chafed command wire trips this 5 A, never O1's 25 A soft
The driver window's H-bridge (K5 / K6) - N16; F8's rating carried (D-471)
The passenger window's H-bridge (K7 / K8) - N16; F9's rating carried (D-471)
K16, the comfort switch, → DP-DCU-P 1, the CU's comfort inlet (N126, N17)
L1-E1 4 - the LS A/C clutch relay's contact feed (N127); no fuse fitted until the swap

potted into the switch's sealed pigtail, so a broken wire still reads as a fault

then, D-368 pattern). D-610: the series resistor sits on the PMU box's board at this wire's end, not in
the harness; D-610: the 47 kΩ baseline stays at the far end, potted into the switch's sealed pigtail, so

No device: the tach cable's shield and drain, cut back and insulated at the coil (L1-E1 15), carried
through here to the PMU box's GND bus (N113, D-556). The shield is grounded at the node only.

Splice at the nose → 14 AWG branch to each lamp plug, terminal RY
Splice at the nose → 14 AWG branch to each lamp plug, terminal RL
Splice at the nose → 12 AWG branch to motor E-03 terminal WR and motor E-04 terminal WR, as the
headlights on L2-F1 1 / 2 (D-487; one feed per motor until then) - each motor's own relay switches it
and its cam stops it (SP-584; confirm at CK08)
Motor E-03 terminal RY - the down command into the motor's own relay (SP-584, D-460); N14 at the
node. A command, not the motor current, but behind O1's 25 A soft fuse, so 14 AWG; in the power
plug because the signal plug had one spare cavity for four commands (D-487)
Splice at the nose → each horn's terminal GY
Front combo lamp F-05, terminal GR
Front combo lamp F-06, terminal GO
Splice at the nose → F-05 RG, F-06 RG, F-12 RG, F-13 RG
#16 Wiper park feed — future motor family
L2-F1-12 · 16 AWG RED · RT09 · capped at the far end
Held as the fused park feed a self-parking motor needs; the bank's always-hot side position F13 is its
protection when it is taken up (D-317)
Motor E-03 terminal R - the up command into the motor's own relay (SP-584, D-460); N12 at the
node; 14 AWG behind O1's 25 A soft fuse (D-487). Was A4's transit contact with its 3.3 kΩ and 47 kΩ
baseline: YG is capped at the motor, and the PMU reads a moving lamp from O1's current
Motor E-04 terminal R - the up command (SP-584, D-460); N13 at the node; 14 AWG (D-487). Was A5's
transit contact: YG is capped at the motor
47 kΩ baseline to the front star ground at the L2-F1 plug (D-368; A4 / A5's baselines are at the
inhibitor switch since D-487) - covers the run to the park contact; a break in the brake branch reads
as brake never pressed. Wiper motor D-02 park terminal L through 12 kΩ. Terminal LB is left
unconnected (capped). D-610: the series resistor sits on the PMU box's board at this wire's end, not
in the harness; D-610: the 47 kΩ baseline stays at the far end, potted into the switch's sealed pigtail,
so a broken wire still reads as a fault
#16 Wiper park return — future motor family
L2-F1-16 · 16 AWG GRY · RT09 · capped at the far end
Run to the wiper branch and left unpinned there: a DIN 72552 motor's park return is pinned into
this cavity at the branch, no leg re-run (D-317)
Motor E-04 terminal RY - the down command (SP-584, D-460); N15 at the node; 14 AWG (D-487). Was
L4-R1 · HDP26-24-21SE / HDP24-24-21PE · mixed-contact circular · PMU box

Carter P4070 + ; pump − → its OWN 12 AWG to the rear star ground

L4-R1-7 · 14 AWG ORN · RT18 · capped at the far end
The hatch-release solenoid's + terminal, through the hinge loop with the tail-lamp conductors — it
exists and is believed to work (Camden 2026-09-08, DV48); fed through K3 in the PMU box, fitted this
L4-R1-8 · 14 AWG ORN · RT25 · capped at the far end
The fuel-door solenoid's + terminal behind the quarter trim — it exists (Camden 2026-09-08, DV49;
K-017 corrected); fed through K4 in the PMU box, fitted this build (D-451, D-370) (D-274)
Interior/spot lamp H-06 LY (00-CAR PT957); the lamp's − through its own DOOR / OFF / ON switch:
ON → roof-rail ground, DOOR → RY to both jamb switches through a 1N4007 each (D-486)
47 kΩ baseline potted in the driver jamb switch's pigtail, to the body at the jamb (G37, D-610), so
all-doors-shut reads 47k and an open wire still reads as a fault
Pulse generator supply — an O10 tap (N73), so the sensor lives and dies with the ICU; sensor
Luggage lamp H-11 +; lamp − → lid switch H-12 → rear star ground
L3-COL · hard-wired at the box, no plug there · PMU box
Ignition switch: ACC → 33 kΩ · IG → 15 kΩ · ST → 6.8 kΩ, all summed onto this wire. D-610: its resistors
and diodes are potted into a short sealed pigtail at the switch - part of the switch, not of the
Light switch E-01: PARK → 33 kΩ · HEAD → 15 kΩ · DIMMER-HI → 8.2 kΩ (fed from the HEAD side) ·
PASS → 3.3 kΩ. D-610: its resistors and diodes are potted into a short sealed pigtail at the switch -
part of the switch, not of the harness
Stalk F-02: LEFT 1.8 kΩ · RIGHT 10 kΩ · OFF 47 kΩ, contacts to column ground. D-610: its resistors and
diodes are potted into a short sealed pigtail at the switch - part of the switch, not of the harness
Stalk D-03: HIGH 4.7 kΩ · LOW 10 kΩ · INT 18 kΩ · OFF 47 kΩ · WASH 470 Ω + 1N4148 (band toward the
contact; R12 / Y2, ladder_a2.cir - the 1.8 kΩ + 1N5819 of D-381 leaked hot and lifted OFF past the fault
line). D-610: its resistors and diodes are potted into a short sealed pigtail at the switch - part of the
Pedal switch F-11 through 4.7 kΩ; other terminal → dash ground. D-610: the series resistor sits on
the PMU box's board at this wire's end, not in the harness
Spare P084 adjustable plunger switch on the brake pedal, fed from the F3 switch supply branched
off L3-COL 10 in the leg through F24 (D-278, D-412)
Horn pad through 8.2 kΩ · wink L NO through 18 kΩ · wink R NO through 33 kΩ — three resistors
joined onto this wire; the two wink resistors sit on the plate board and reach it on J2 pin 3 through
DP-CUR 7 (D-499, D-504, D-521). D-610: the horn pad's 8.2 kΩ sits on the PMU box's board; the winks'
Ignition switch B terminal · light switch E-01 common through F24 in the PMU box after F3, on its
Light switch common and the brake-wake
Light switch E-01 common and the brake plunger (DV19, DV25)
Wiper stalk D-03 WASH contact (same terminal as the WASH ladder leg); contact's other side →
Parking brake switch → brake warning lamp
Parking brake switch C-04 terminal BR (switch body grounds through the lever bracket)
Kick-down switch B-32 at the throttle pedal, one terminal. Ignition-fed off O12 through its own
inline fuse - never off F3, whose 5 A also carries the ignition switch, the light switch and the wake
L3-DASH · hard-wired at the box, no plug there · PMU box
Dash illumination lamps E-06, E-07, E-10 (RL) + head unit illumination wire - O20 is the illumination
bus only, on with PARK / HEAD, plain on/off; the lamps are dimmed through their return on
Glove box lamp H-01 +; lamp − → lid switch H-02 → dash ground
L3-HU · hard-wired at the box, no plug there · PMU box
Head unit red (ACC) wire; USB-C module +
